subject: maths

concepts.title: Identifying Direct and Inverse Variation
concepts.definition: Analyzing real-life situation data pairs to establish whether an increase in one variable leads to a proportional change in another.
concepts.formula: direct: x/y = k, inverse: x*y = k
concepts.key_idea: Direct variation requires a constant ratio between quantities, whereas inverse variation requires a constant product.
question_patterns: determine whether the given quantities vary directly or inversely
check if the relationship between parking time and charges is in direct proportion
identify if the speed of a car and time taken are inversely proportional
examine whether the area of land and crop harvested are directly proportional
verify if the number of workers and time taken to complete a job are inversely proportional

solution_steps.explain: Calculate the ratio x/y for direct variation or product x*y for inverse variation across data pairs.
Check if the computed values remain constant for all corresponding data pairs in the table.
If the ratio x/y is constant, the quantities are in direct proportion; if the product x*y is constant, they are in inverse proportion.

concepts.title: Direct Proportion Quantity Calculation
concepts.definition: Determining an unknown value of a variable when two quantities maintain a fixed ratio across changes.
concepts.key_idea: In direct proportion, the quotient of corresponding values remains invariant.
question_patterns: calculate the cost of cloth for a given length using direct proportion
find the height of a tree casting a shadow of known length
how many sheets of paper will weigh a given mass in grams
determine the distance travelled by a train in a given time at uniform speed
what is the number of bottles filled in a specified time by a machine

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the second value of the first variable by the first value of the second variable.
Divide the cross product by the initial quantity of the first variable to obtain the target value.
Confirm that y2/x2 equals y1/x1, ensuring the quotient remains invariant for direct proportion.

concepts.title: Scale Ratio and Map Distance Applications
concepts.definition: Calculating actual geographic distances or map representations based on a given scale factor ratio.
concepts.key_idea: Map representation distances and actual ground distances are directly proportional.
question_patterns: find the actual distance between two cities given map scale and map distance
calculate the map representation distance given actual distance and scale
determine the actual length of an object given its enlarged photograph scale
what is the ground distance corresponding to a specified length on a scale map
evaluate the actual distance when map scale ratio is given

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the measured map length by the scale multiplier to determine actual ground distance.
If the scale is in cm and the answer is required in km, divide by 100000 to convert centimetres to kilometres.
Check that the ratio of actual distance to map distance equals the scale factor for all pairs, confirming direct proportion.

concepts.title: Inverse Proportion Quantity Calculation
concepts.definition: Computing an unknown variable when two quantities vary such that their product remains constant.
concepts.key_idea: In inverse proportion, an increase in one variable produces a proportional decrease in the other.
question_patterns: calculate time required to fill a tank with a reduced number of pipes
find how long food provisions will last if more students join a hostel
determine the number of workers needed to complete a task in fewer hours
what is the angle between consecutive spokes on a wheel with a given number of spokes
how many boxes are needed if each box contains a specified number of items

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the initial value of the first variable by the initial value of the second variable.
Divide the constant product k by the new value of the first variable to get the target quantity.
Confirm that x2 * y2 equals k, ensuring the product remains invariant for inverse proportion.

worked_examples.question_pattern: The cost of {x1} metres of cloth is {y1}. Find the cost of {x2} metres of cloth.

solution_template.explain: Multiply the new length x2 by the original cost y1.
Divide the result by original length x1.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A pole of height {x1} metres casts a shadow of {y1} metres. Find the height of a tree casting a shadow of {y2_given} metres.

solution_template.explain: Multiply shadow length x2 by object height y1.
Divide by initial shadow length x1 to find tree height.

worked_examples.question_pattern: The scale of a map is given as 1 : {scale_factor}. Two cities are {map_distance} cm apart on the map. Find the actual distance.

solution_template.explain: Multiply map distance by the scale factor.

worked_examples.question_pattern: {x1} pipes fill a tank in {y1} minutes. How long will it take if only {x2} pipes are used?

solution_template.explain: Multiply initial number of pipes by initial time in minutes.
Divide total pipe-minutes by the new number of pipes.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Food provision for {x1} students lasts {y1} days. How long will it last for {x2} students?

solution_template.explain: Divide total provision days by the new number of students.

questions: 1. Check if the parking charges near a railway station for 4 hours (Rs 60), 8 hours (Rs 100), 12 hours (Rs 140) and 24 hours (Rs 180) are in direct proportion to the parking time.
2. A mixture of paint is prepared by mixing 1 part of red pigments with 8 parts of base. Find the parts of base needed for 4, 7, 12, and 20 parts of red pigment.
3. If 1 part of a red pigment requires 75 mL of base, how much red pigment should we mix with 1800 mL of base?
Attempt this end-of-chapter task in your own words and support your answer with reasoning about bottles.
5. A photograph of a bacteria enlarged 50,000 times attains a length of 5 cm. What is the actual length of the bacteria? If enlarged 20,000 times, what is its length?
6. In a model of a ship, the mast is 9 cm high while the actual ship mast is 12 m high. If the length of the ship is 28 m, how long is the model ship?
7. Suppose 2 kg of sugar contains 9 x 10^6 crystals. How many crystals are in 5 kg and 1.2 kg of sugar?
8. Rashmi has a road map with a scale of 1 cm representing 18 km. She drives for 72 km. What is her distance covered on the map?
9. A 5 m 60 cm high vertical pole casts a shadow 3 m 20 cm long. Find the shadow cast by a pole 10 m 50 cm high, and the height of a pole casting a shadow 5 m long.
10. A loaded truck travels 14 km in 25 minutes. If speed remains constant, how far can it travel in 5 hours?

1. Which of the following are in inverse proportion: (i) number of workers and time taken (ii) time taken and distance covered at uniform speed (iii) cultivated land area and crop harvested (iv) journey time and speed (v) population and land area per person.
2. In a TV game show, prize money of Rs 1,00,000 is divided equally among winners. Find individual prize amounts for 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, and 20 winners.
3. Rehman is making a wheel using spokes. Calculate the angle between consecutive spokes for 8, 10, 12, and 15 spokes, and find spokes needed for an angle of 40 degrees.
4. If a box of sweets is divided among 24 children, they get 5 sweets each. How many would each get if the number of children is reduced by 4?
5. A farmer has food to feed 20 animals for 6 days. How long would the food last if there were 10 more animals?
6. A contractor estimates 3 persons rewire a house in 4 days. How long should 4 persons take to complete the job?
7. A batch of bottles was packed in 25 boxes with 12 bottles each. How many boxes are needed if packed with 20 bottles per box?
8. A factory requires 42 machines to produce articles in 63 days. How many machines are required to produce the same articles in 54 days?
9. A car takes 2 hours travelling at 60 km/h. How long will it take at 80 km/h?
10. Two persons fit new windows in 3 days. (i) How long would 1 person take? (ii) How many persons are needed to finish in 1 day?
11. A school has 8 periods a day of 45 minutes duration. How long would each period be if the school has 9 periods for the same total duration?
